language.script_notes: This is Mexico's most indigenous region — Zapotec, Mixtec, Tzotzil, Tzeltal and other languages are widely spoken, and traditional dress is often visible. Teachers'-union (CNTE) political graffiti is common on walls.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Steel W-beam on the main roads; many mountain roads have none, with frequent landslide scars and 'derrumbes' signs.
road_furniture.line_paint: Patchy — main highways marked, but many roads are narrow, winding and unmarked; 'topes' everywhere, often unmarked and severe.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted kerbs and cobbles in the colonial towns; little kerbing in villages.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Octagonal or crucifix concrete poles. Fewer OXXOs than the centre and north; more small independent shops and roadside stalls.

architecture.roof_style: Flat concrete roofs with tinacos in towns; corrugated sheet and palm thatch in poorer and hotter areas; clay tile in the colonial highlands.
architecture.roof_material: Concrete slab, corrugated metal, palm thatch, some clay tile.
architecture.wall_construction: More adobe, brick and simple block than the rest of Mexico, a lot of it unfinished; carved-stone colonial buildings in Oaxaca and San Cristóbal de las Casas.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Bare block and adobe browns, plus strong colours on colonial and market-town facades.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Colonial Oaxaca and highland San Cristóbal; simple adobe and block village houses; palm-thatch huts in the hot lowlands; visible poverty and self-built housing on steep slopes.

nature.vegetation: Tropical dry forest and pine-oak on the slopes; lush cloud forest and rainforest in the Chiapas highlands and the Lacandon; coffee plantations on the mountainsides; coconut palms and mangroves on the Guerrero and Oaxaca coasts.
nature.terrain: Rugged, tightly folded mountains — the Sierra Madre del Sur and the Chiapas highlands — dropping steeply to a narrow Pacific coastal plain, with the flat, fiercely windy Isthmus of Tehuantepec (wind farms) between them.
nature.climate_signature: Hot and humid in the lowlands, cooler and wet in the highlands, greener and rainier overall than central or northern Mexico.

vehicles.plate_color: State plates for Oaxaca, Chiapas and Guerrero, each with its own design and banner.
vehicles.plate_format: State-dependent, commonly three letters and three–four digits.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Older, more worn cars and pickups; 'camionetas' (pickup trucks) used as rural passenger transport; three-wheeled mototaxis in lowland towns.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Coverage thins out in the mountains; many minor roads unmapped.

confusion_set.shared_traits: The Chiapas highlands run straight into Guatemala — same volcanic mountains, milpa farming, Maya communities and climate
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Mexican state plates, OXXO, 'topes' signage and the bar-free camera car; Guatemala has uniform plates, US-style school buses and rougher roads.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country — colonial towns, pine-oak highlands, ALTO, tinacos
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The south is poorer and rougher — more adobe, corrugated roofs, unpaved and landslide-prone roads, visible indigenous dress and union graffiti, and more jungle; the centre is a prosperous temperate plateau with volcanoes and agave.
